UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF VIRGINIA ALEXANDRIA DIVISION

MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE,

Plaintiff,  v.  KATIE HALL, individually; NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED CHILDREN; META PLATFORMS, INC.; and JOHN/JANE DOES 1–6,

Defendants. ____________________________________/

Case No. 1:26-cv-02331

[PROPOSED] ORDER

This matter is before the Court on Plaintiff’s Motion for Priority Determination and Sequencing of Pending Proceedings Concerning ECF No. 96 (ECF No. ___) (the “Motion”). Upon consideration of the Motion, the Memorandum in Support, any response and reply, and the record, and for good cause shown, it is hereby

ORDERED as follows:

1.	The Motion is GRANTED. The Court has given the Motion priority consideration and determines it on the papers under Local Civil Rule 7(J) and Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 78(b).

2.	To the extent authorized under the operative referral, Magistrate Judge William E. Fitzpatrick shall give priority consideration to Plaintiff’s Rule 54(b) Motion to Vacate ECF No. 96 and Determine Magistrate Judge Davis’s Ownership of Meta Common Stock (ECF No. ___) (the “Rule 54(b) Motion”).

3.	Final determination by the District Judge of the following matters (the “Overlapping ECF No. 96 Issues”) is DEFERRED until disposition of the Rule 54(b) Motion or further order of the District Judge:

(a)	whether ECF No. 96 should be set aside, modified, or given limited effect, as requested in ECF Nos. 97–99; and

(b)	the historical ownership and holding-arrangement facts identified in ECF No. 93 ¶ 5, with any relief under ECF No. 93 that depends on them.

4.	Upon disposition of the Rule 54(b) Motion, the District Judge will complete review of the Overlapping ECF No. 96 Issues with that disposition available. That disposition remains subject to timely objection under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 72(a).

5.	The District Judge retains authority over the referral. Nothing in this Order limits the District Judge’s determination at any time of any independent or threshold issue. Those issues include the referral and successor-designation questions presented in ECF No. 93 ¶ 10(R1) and ECF No. 97 ¶¶ 15 and 20(6), and independently warranted relief under ECF No. 93. If the District Judge determines that the Rule 54(b) Motion falls outside the operative referral, the deferral in paragraph 3 ends upon that determination.

6.	This Order does not stay this action. It does not defer or decide ECF Nos. 10, 21, or 45. No pending objection or motion is withdrawn. No deadline is extended or restarted. The briefing on ECF No. 93 is not reopened.

The Clerk’s Office is directed to provide a copy of this Order to pro se Plaintiff at his last known address.

Alexandria, Virginia

__________, 2026

______________________________

Rossie D. Alston, Jr.

United States District Judge
